name: Shakti back-and-forth: amygdala signal right, then left
origin: Todd Murphy (Shakti software), after Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity theory
summary: Murphy's 'interhemispheric intrusion' (back-and-forth) session: 30 min of the amygdala burst-firing signal over the right temporal lobe, its 'usually wrong' side, then 30 min over the left. Murphy says the first phase is expected to be unpleasant and that the switch can bring bliss or elation.
setting: Advanced users only, after a side test has shown the usual pattern for the signal (this file assumes the usual sides). The vendor says darkness and silence (sensory deprivation) help; eyes closed, relaxed. Run murphy-shakti-test-session-amygdala first.
schedule: Vendor rules: never on consecutive days, at most every 72 hours or weekly; 60-minute sessions at most once in 3 weeks.
notes: Murphy bases the design on Persinger's vectorial hemisphericity idea: stimulating a structure's negative counterpart first mutes the positive one, and stimulating the positive one next gives what he calls a 'sudden burst'. For the amygdala he links this to the anterior commissure and to bliss and elation. That the right amygdala is the unpleasant side rests on user reports and a small Persinger-lab study (Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992: burst-firing over the right temporal lobe raised apprehension in women). Murphy links the right amygdala with fear and sadness and the left with bliss, mostly from user reports, so phase 1 can bring fear. Phase 1 is meant to be unpleasant (the vendor: 'EXPECTED to be unpleasant') and phase 2 pleasant; if phase 1 feels good instead, the vendor reads that as a possible 'reversed' or 'left-handed' structure. The vendor 'strongly' suggests running this procedure with each signal separately (murphy-shakti-back-and-forth-amygdala and -hippocampus) before trying the two-signal option (murphy-shakti-back-and-forth-both). If phase 1 becomes too uncomfortable, press Skip at once to start phase 2, but never stop after phase 1 without phase 2 (the vendor: 'Do NOT apply the signal over the wrong side without following it with the same signal over the correct side'). For unwanted effects that linger, the vendor's undo procedures are the hippocampal signal over both frontal lobes or the ERP signal over the cerebellum (in this project: murphy-shakti-cerebellum-erp). Coils: a cross of four over each temporal lobe (FT7, C5, TP7, T9 and FT8, C6, TP8, T10); each phase drives the four coils of one side together, without movement or channel alternation (none is described for this procedure). The vendor's Alternative procedures page says to apply the signal 'over the (usually) WRONG side of your head for 30 minutes, and then immediately apply the same wave form to the (usually) CORRECT side', without a length for the second phase; its 30 min here is an inference (it matches the first phase and the 30 + 30 min the page gives for the two-signal option; the Bliss page gives 20-30 min per phase). The amygdala ('burstx') file is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz), 230 points at the vendor's standard 3-ms points (0.69 s), followed by the vendor's standard latency of about 4 s. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition. If phase 1 is distressing, skip to phase 2 as the vendor advises; stop the session if distress continues in phase 2. Revised after a re-check of the procedures page (2026): the length of phase 2 is now marked as an inference, and the page's advice on order and on 'reversed' structures is added; sites, signals and timing are unchanged and remain approximations as described.

Phase 2: amygdala signal, LEFT side ('usually correct')
